scope: Root application-owned ingestion executor lifecycle shutdown

criteria.description: The default root factory reproduces a lifecycle defect: closing the ASGI TestClient leaves the application-owned ingestion executor unshut and its worker thread alive
criteria.limitations: The baseline is local and process-bound; it is not a production shutdown or distributed-worker claim

criteria.description: The correction is reversible and local: the default factory owns only resources it constructs, injected providers remain caller-owned, shutdown is idempotent, queued work is cancelled safely, and private cleanup/resource ordering is preserved
criteria.limitations: The gate authorizes implementation and verification only; it does not accept shutdown behavior

criteria.description: A deterministic regression path exists for TestClient lifespan close, completed and queued uploads, resource ownership, idempotent shutdown, and preserved Phase 1.6/CI checks before a fresh independent review
criteria.limitations: External process supervisors, distributed workers, crash recovery and deployment shutdown remain outside this local task

authority.scope: Root application-owned ingestion executor lifecycle shutdown
authority.decision: Authorize only reversible local lifecycle implementation, fault-injection verification and fresh independent review; no external effect or release acceptance
authority.expires_or_revalidates: Revalidate on resource ownership, app lifespan, executor, journal, storage, worker or deployment scope changes

next_action: Install an application-owned ASGI lifespan shutdown hook and verify local executor/resource lifecycle without changing caller-owned provider ownership
revalidation_triggers: Root factory or ingestion executor ownership changes
Job journal, knowledge store, vector store or audit resource close semantics change
External worker, deployment or distributed recovery scope is introduced
A new probe shows shutdown can leak work, close caller-owned resources or lose private cleanup references
